content.text: All preferred elements are present. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: Section 13 meets our preferred licence position in full, so no redline is warranted. 13.1 grants the hosted-Services rights to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" (with Authorized Users permitted), and 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, including contractor support. 13.3 limits Vendor's ability to revoke or suspend to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity, and permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor, backed by the Customer-favourable assignment right in 24.1 (Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent) and 24.4 (no Vendor termination/repricing on Customer change of control). Nothing is revocable at Vendor's discretion and there are no named-user or territory limits cutting across the Order Forms; the restrictions in 13.4 are ordinary conduct limits that expressly preserve use of Customer Data and output. Minor note only, not a deviation: 13.3 frames the revocation limit around a "payment or use breach affecting the licensed item" rather than any uncured material breach, which is narrower than the general standard and therefore favourable to us.
